links.comparator_used: Single-modality (accelerometer-only) CNN and LSTM models; ablation removing one sensor modality at a time
links.outcome: Test-set accuracy and AUC for fall risk classification
links.effect: Multimodal CNN-LSTM without attention 91.0% accuracy, AUC 0.948 vs accelerometer-only CNN 86.3% (AUC 0.911) and LSTM 85.9% (AUC 0.908). Full four-modality model 94.2% (AUC 0.967). Removing accelerometer gave 86.4%, gyroscope 90.1%, plantar pressure 90.9%, heart rate/HRV 92.3%.
links.quote: The multimodal fusion model without attention mechanisms achieves notable gains over single-modality approaches, supporting the value of integrating heterogeneous sensor information for broader risk characterization

links.comparator_used: Passive-monitoring group wearing identical sensors with data logging only (no alerts)
links.outcome: Fall incidence over a three-month field deployment (exploratory)
links.effect: 0.82 vs 2.14 falls per person-month; RR 0.38 (95% CI 0.24-0.62); total falls 12 vs 34; reported as 62% fewer falls
links.tradeoff: Non-randomized, unblinded and confounded by daily risk summaries and caregiver notifications. The authors state it is not evidence of causal effect. Alert false positive rate was 8.2% (134 false alarms among 1,634 alerts).
links.quote: In a subsequent three-month deployment with 80 participants, the group receiving active alerts recorded 62% fewer falls than the passive-monitoring control group (0.82 vs. 2.14 falls per person-month; p < 0.01).

links.comparator_used: Passive-monitoring group with data logging only, no alerts or caregiver notification
links.outcome: Fall incidence over a three-month field deployment (exploratory)
links.effect: 0.82 vs 2.14 falls per person-month; RR 0.38 (95% CI 0.24-0.62); near-falls prevented (self-reported) 27 vs 8
links.tradeoff: Caregiver notification was bundled with other intervention components (daily risk summaries), so its effect cannot be isolated. The design was non-randomized and exploratory. Alert false positive rate was 8.2%.
links.quote: In a subsequent three-month deployment with 80 participants, the group receiving active alerts recorded 62% fewer falls than the passive-monitoring control group (0.82 vs. 2.14 falls per person-month; p < 0.01).

design_hint: active real-time alerts vs passive monitoring
